richSourceDetails: Original IM2021 Grade5 U05:L10 Solve Problems with Decimals uses a printed FIVE-ATHLETE LUGE TABLE (instructional dataset, not asserted live results), records time in SECONDS to thousandths and top speed in MILES PER HOUR to hundredths, then compares how different rounding precision can create ties. Faster race means smaller elapsed time; greater top speed is a different comparison.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder The Luge includes original photograph attributed Kris Krüg CC BY-SA2.0; do not copy source photo without image/rights verification. Original published table times/speeds: Athlete1=48.532s/82.13mph; A2=48.561s/82.75mph; A3=48.626s/82.81mph; A4=48.634s/83.07mph; A5=48.708s/82.80mph.

Activity 1 How Accurate Is It?: original all five times round to49 seconds nearest WHOLE, giving a five-way time tie; nearest TENTH times A1=48.5,A2=48.6,A3=48.6,A4=48.6,A5=48.7, so A2–A4 tie; nearest HUNDREDTH A1=48.53,A2=48.56,A3=48.63,A4=48.63,A5=48.71, so A3/A4 tie. Real winner by full precision is A1 (48.532s) fastest.

Source asks possible time values to nearest THOUSANDTH when displayed nearest hundredth as48.85s: conventional half-up range48.845 through48.854 inclusive in 0.001 steps. Another time48.615 recorded nearest thousandth rounds to48.62 to nearest hundredth. Students interpret rounding interval not invent one exact underlying time.

Activity 2 Compare Speeds: original descending fastest top speeds A4 83.07 >A3 82.81 >A5 82.80 >A2 82.75 >A1 82.13mph. Nearest TENTH mph A1=82.1,A2=82.8,A3=82.8,A4=83.1,A5=82.8, so A2/A3/A5 tie; nearest WHOLE mph A1=82, A2–A5=83. A sixth athlete strictly faster than82.80 but slower than82.81 may have82.805mph to thousandths, with many other valid values.
